master_predictions.verdict: On the six demands: (1) long life — 'according to natural Causes, he might live many yeers', nature being strong and he subject to few diseases; (2) Ireland would well agree with his constitution and he might get honour there; (3) his younger years would be the most pleasant of all his whole life; (4) past accidents recited (and confessed): molestation concerning lands or his wife's jointure/portion, great variance with his wife, and want of money for about six months before the question; (5)–(6) future: a treaty with some nobleman about the education of his child or children, support for about three years and three quarters, and then danger of losing his life, goods, lands and fortune, timed by the Moon wanting 7°22′ of the opposition of Mars.
reasoning_points: Finding the Ascendant not vitiated by Saturn (lord of the sixth) or Jupiter (lord of the eighth), the lord of the Ascendant (the Sun) in his exaltation, unimpeded and swift in the ninth, the Moon applying to a trine of Jupiter in mid-heaven, and the fortunate planets angular and more potent than the infortunes — long life
The Moon applying to Jupiter, the planet in the house of honours, and Jupiter placed in the sign which signifies Ireland — he was advised Ireland would agree with him and he might get honour there
The two fortunes in the tenth and the Sun and another in the ninth — his younger years the most pleasant; Mars in the eighth about the 24th–26th year of his age — crosses first beginning then

The Moon in the querent's second applying to Jupiter, lord of the fifth (children), and then to a trine of the lord of the eighth (the wife's substance) — a salary or treaty with a nobleman for the education of his children, settled out of the wife's fortune or jointure
The Moon separated from Mercury, lord of the second, by 6°21′ — want of money for about six moneths before the question (confessed)
The Moon wanting 7°22′ of the true opposition of Mars (Mars lord of the fourth, in the eighth) — after some three years and three quarters, danger to life, goods, lands and fortune
master_predictions.outcome: Recorded severally in the chapter: of long life, 'This hath hitherto proved true; he being yet alive this present, March 1646'; 'the Querent did go into Ireland, and there performed good service and obtained a notable Victory against the Rebels'; the children-education treaty 'he did settle before he went out of England'; after the timed period 'he was in severall actions both dangerous to his Person and Fortune', had honourable employment on his Majesty's part, 'yet is he now for ever, by Sentence of the Parliament, deprived of so much happinesse, as to end his dayes in England'. The past accidents (the wife's jointure variance, the six months' want of money) are marked 'This was confessed' / 'This was confessed also' in the text.

master_predictions.verdict: 'I judged the absent Brother was alive and had no manner of casualty happened unto him, but was in good health'; the querent would hear of him that very day (by the carriers of those countries); and he would come home within less than one week.
reasoning_points: Venus, significatrix of the brother (lady of the third), in no manner of way afflicted either by Mercury, lord of the eighth, or by Mars; the Moon's separation good (from a dexter trine of Jupiter) and her next application favourable — the absent alive and in health

Venus, significatrix of the quesited, and Saturn, lord of the Ascendant, applying to each other by a friendly trine which perfected that very day (five o'clock by the ephemeris, a little after four by the London meridian) — the querent should hear news of his brother very suddenly, that very day
Venus leaving a northern sign and entering a south sign — he was coming homewards towards his own house
The nature of the significators' sign and degrees in this question denoting a week — his return within less than one week
master_predictions.outcome: 'He hath since confidently affirmed, that about the very moment of time... a Carrier came casually to his house, and informed him his Brother was in health and living'; and 'he came home the Tuesday following, when the Moon came to [Venus]'.

master_predictions.verdict: 'You see here are eight testimonies of a Male Conception, or of Being with child of a Son; and but four of a Female; I therefore affirmed, that the Lady was impregnated of a Man child'; and, giving for every degree one week, 'that about fourteen weeks from the time of the Question, she should be delivered'.
reasoning_points: Plurality of masculine testimonies (eight) over feminine (four) among the proper significators — sign ascending, sign of the fifth, lord of the fifth, lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, the lord of the hour, and their signs and houses

The signs of the fifth are moveable, arguing a short time; but Saturn, lord of the fifth, being a ponderous planet of slow motion, and the Moon posited in the sign of the fifth, were much valued in the timing

The Moon's distance from the opposition of Saturn is 14°47′, and Mercury's distance from the body of Saturn 13°37′ — the two differing by only 1°10′, a degree was given for a week: about fourteen weeks
